idiom_name: class over mutableMapOf with a MutableList<Operation> journal
implementation_notes: A Kotlin class backed by mutableMapOf implements the collaborator with working behaviour and appends each received operation to a MutableList<Operation>; the declaration mechanics are ordinary Kotlin, so nothing of the classic double structure has to be built, and the test-only accessor can be an internal method or a separate test-facing interface. MockK records interactions on mocks and spies - verify { }, capture(slot), confirmVerified - but does not implement behaviour, so it covers the spy and mock rows; if a mock must also behave, delegate its answers to a hand-written fake. Thread-safety is not provided: a fake used from coroutines needs a Mutex or concurrent structures. Keep the fake per test - a companion-object or top-level fake is shared by the whole suite - and return journal.toList() so callers cannot mutate the journal.
pitfalls: mutableMapOf and MutableList are not thread-safe; a fake exercised from Dispatchers.Default needs a Mutex or concurrent collections.
A fake held in a companion object or a top-level property is shared across tests - create it per test.
Expecting MockK-style verification (verify, capture) from a hand-written fake means the wrong double was chosen; those facilities belong to mocks and spies.
